transcript.content:
I attempted to create measurements_normalized_v2 but the database returned the same operational error as before: "object name reserved for internal use: sqlite_sequence". That error is coming from SQLite internals when attempting write DDL/DML, so my code cannot create or modify tables in the current DB session.

What I can do now
- Confirm exactly which normalized rows would be written (SELECT-only, read-only operations work).
- Provide the exact CREATE + INSERT statements you can run once the DB write issue is fixed (or I can run them for you once you give DB write access / the sqlite_sequence error is resolved).
- Suggest steps to diagnose/fix the sqlite_sequence / write-permission problem.

Preview of the normalized rows (what I would insert)
Here is the SELECT I used to assemble the normalized rows (read-only — this shows what will be inserted for all measurements with status='valid'):

SELECT
  session_id,
  participant_id,
  condition,
  'cognitive_score' AS metric,
  cognitive_score AS value,
  'points' AS units,
  recorded_at,
  status,
  notes AS source_notes
FROM measurements
WHERE status='valid';

If you want both cognitive_score and reaction_ms normalized as separate rows per session, use this UNION version (recommended):

SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, 'cognitive_score' AS metric, cognitive_score AS value, 'points' AS units, recorded_at, status, notes AS source_notes
FROM measurements
WHERE status='valid'
UNION ALL
SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, 'reaction_ms' AS metric, reaction_ms AS value, 'ms' AS units, recorded_at, status, notes AS source_notes
FROM measurements
WHERE status='valid';

SQL statements to create and populate measurements_normalized_v2
Run these once the DB write problem is resolved:

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS measurements_normalized_v2 (
  measurement_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  session_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  participant_id TEXT,
  condition TEXT,
  metric TEXT NOT NULL,
  value REAL,
  units TEXT,
  recorded_at TEXT,
  status TEXT,
  source_notes TEXT
);

INSERT INTO measurements_normalized_v2 (session_id, participant_id, condition, metric, value, units, recorded_at, status, source_notes)
SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, 'cognitive_score', cognitive_score, 'points', recorded_at, status, notes FROM measurements WHERE status='valid';

-- If you also want reaction time as separate measurements, run:
INSERT INTO measurements_normalized_v2 (session_id, participant_id, condition, metric, value, units, recorded_at, status, source_notes)
SELECT session_id, participant_id, condition, 'reaction_ms', reaction_ms, 'ms', recorded_at, status, notes FROM measurements WHERE status='valid';

How to diagnose/fix the sqlite_sequence error
- Check file permissions: ensure the DB file is writable by the process/user running these statements.
- Check for locked connections: verify no other process is holding an exclusive lock or long transaction.
- Inspect sqlite_sequence table only if necessary: sometimes sqlite_sequence can become corrupted. As an admin, you can:
  - Run PRAGMA integrity_check; to detect corruption.
  - If sqlite_sequence is the issue and you are comfortable with it, a possible repair sequence (admin only) is:
    - VACUUM;
    - or if needed (careful): PRAGMA writable_schema=ON; DELETE FROM sqlite_sequence WHERE name='measurements_normalized_v2'; PRAGMA writable_schema=OFF;
  - Note: the above direct sqlite_sequence edits are advanced and should be run by a DB admin with backups in place.

Next step (pick one)
- I can re-attempt creation/insert now if you want (but it will likely fail until the sqlite_sequence issue is fixed).
- I can run the UNION ALL SELECT and return the exact rows that would be inserted (preview), including counts and samples.
- I can provide a CSV export of the SELECT results for you to import elsewhere.
